Let $p$ be the price (dollars) and $N$ the tickets sold. $N$ is linear in $p$ with slope $-\dfrac{45}{1.12}\approx-40.179$ tickets per dollar, and $N(10)=800$:
\[N(p)=800-\frac{45}{1.12}(p-10)=1201.786-40.179\,p.\]
Revenue is price times tickets:
\[R(p)=p\,N(p)=1201.786\,p-40.179\,p^2,\]
a downward parabola. Its maximum is at the vertex
\[p=\frac{1201.786}{2(40.179)}\approx 14.96.\]
\textbf{Answer:} set the price at about \boxed{\$14.96} (about 601 tickets, revenue $\approx\$8{,}987$).
2:
The chain moves at the same linear speed over both sprockets. Front sprocket: $30$ rev/min $=60\pi$ rad/min, radius $9$ in, so the chain speed is
\[v=9(60\pi)=540\pi\ \text{in/min}.\]
Rear sprocket (radius 4 in) angular speed: $\omega=\dfrac{540\pi}{4}=135\pi\approx424.1$ rad/min.
The rear wheel turns with the rear sprocket, so its rim moves at $R\omega=5500$ in/min:
\[R=\frac{5500}{135\pi}\approx \boxed{12.97\ \text{inches}}.\]
3:
One lap takes 95 s at 5 m/s, so the circumference is $475$ m and the radius is $r=\dfrac{475}{2\pi}\approx75.60$ m.

$8.5$ min $=510$ s $=5(95)+35$ s, so after 5 full laps she has run another $35(5)=175$ m along the track from her starting point. That arc subtends
\[\theta=\frac{175}{r}\approx2.3149\ \text{rad}.\]
The straight-line distance between two points on a circle separated by angle $\theta$ is the chord $2r\sin(\theta/2)$:
\[d=2(75.60)\sin(1.1574)\approx \boxed{138.5\ \text{m}}.\]
(The 91 s fact only places her start just past the northernmost point; it doesn't change this distance.)

\textbf{(a)} $g(2x)=-3$ when $2x\le10$, i.e. $x\le5$, and $g(2x)=\sqrt{2x}$ when $x>5$. Then $h(u)=u^2+4$ gives
\[h(g(2x))=\begin{cases}(-3)^2+4=13, & x\le5\\[2pt] (\sqrt{2x})^2+4=2x+4, & x>5\end{cases}\]
\textbf{(b)}
\[\frac{h(3a)-h(2a)}{a}=\frac{(9a^2+4)-(4a^2+4)}{a}=\frac{5a^2}{a}=\boxed{5a}\quad(a\ne0).\]
5:
Let $h$ be the height and $d$ Fred's first distance from the building. Then
\[h=d\tan38^\circ\quad\text{and}\quad h=(d+100)\tan34^\circ.\]
Setting these equal: $d(\tan38^\circ-\tan34^\circ)=100\tan34^\circ$, so
\[d=\frac{100\tan34^\circ}{\tan38^\circ-\tan34^\circ}\approx631.70\ \text{ft},\qquad h=d\tan38^\circ\approx\boxed{493.5\ \text{ft}}.\]
6:
Max $52$ at $t=2$, min $-108$ at $t=7.6$: half a period is $5.6$ h, so the period is $11.2$ h. Midline $\frac{52+(-108)}{2}=-28$, amplitude $80$. Starting at the max:
\[T(t)=-28+80\cos\!\Big(\frac{2\pi}{11.2}(t-2)\Big).\]
$T<10\iff\cos\!\big(\frac{2\pi}{11.2}(t-2)\big)<\frac{38}{80}=0.475$. With $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(0.475)\approx1.0758$, this happens when $\frac{2\pi}{11.2}(t-2)$ lies between $\alpha$ and $2\pi-\alpha$ (plus multiples of $2\pi$), i.e. for
\[t\in(3.918,\,11.282)\ \text{and}\ (15.118,\,22.482)\ \text{and (just at the start)}\ [0,\,0.082).\]
Total time below $10^\circ$C in the first 24 hours:
\[7.365+7.365+0.082\approx\boxed{14.8\ \text{hours}}.\]
7:
Newberg: $N(t)=1325\cdot4^{t/15}$ ($t$ in years after Jan 1, 2000). So $N(5)=1325\cdot4^{1/3}\approx2103.3$ and Kowplunc then had $2N(5)\approx4206.6$.

Kowplunc grows exponentially: $K(t)=550\,b^t$ with $550\,b^5=4206.6$, so $b=(7.6484)^{1/5}\approx1.50215$.

Solve $550\,b^t=20000$:
\[t=\frac{\ln(20000/550)}{\ln b}=\frac{\ln 36.364}{\ln1.50215}\approx\boxed{8.83\ \text{years after Jan 1, 2000}}.\]

\textbf{(a)} Direction from $(10,15)$ to $(6,-2)$ is $\langle-4,-17\rangle$, length $\sqrt{305}\approx17.464$. Moving 2 m/s:
\[x(t)=10-\frac{8}{\sqrt{305}}t\approx10-0.458t,\qquad y(t)=15-\frac{34}{\sqrt{305}}t\approx15-1.947t.\]
\textbf{(b)} Iseult covers $\langle-17,-2\rangle$ in 8 s:
\[x(t)=18-\frac{17}{8}t,\qquad y(t)=3-\frac14 t.\]
\textbf{(c)} $x(t)=0\Rightarrow t=\frac{8\cdot18}{17}=\frac{144}{17}\approx\boxed{8.47\ \text{s}}$ (continuing on the same line past $(1,1)$, at the point $(0,\,0.88)$).
